title: Sparse Minimax Estimation of Indirect Provider Excess Effects across Many Providers
banked_reason: kernel_substituted: proposed universal matched supplied-pilot frontier remains open on fixed finite covariate spaces with at least two points
gap_reasons: The proposed matched supplied-pilot frontier is delivered only on fixed infinite spaces (and the separate fixed-Lebesgue subclass); for fixed finite spaces with at least two points this headline theorem leaves the nuisance modulus open, so re-scope the flagship claim or supply that missing characterization.
The sharp nuisance modulus for finite spaces with at least two points remains open, so the advertised boundary is incomplete precisely in that cardinality regime.
The projected paper-score gate caps the graded field tier at subfield: 7.2 < 7.4.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved a universal sampling/product risk bracket, a singleton obstruction to a universal nuisance floor, and a matched nuisance-aware rate on fixed infinite and fixed-Lebesgue spaces. The originally proposed same-class universal matched frontier failed on finite covariate spaces with at least two points; their nuisance modulus remains open. The final math panel passed, but the decision panel found kernel substitution and the cold-tier score ceiling was 7.2 below the 7.4 field threshold. Eight proof bases became mechanically stale after deleting a vacuous pilot-independence assumption; their proof texts remain present, but the graph is not mechanically all-proved.
tldr: For every arbitrary fixed standard measurable covariate space, the feasible clipped empirical-ratio and sparse-projection estimator gives the universal weighted-risk upper bound \((s/k)\min\{1,k\log(ek/s)/n+\delta^2\epsilon^2\}\), while the credited paired sampling mechanism gives the universal lower bound \((s/k)\min\{1,k\log(ek/s)/n\}\); these bounds match when \(\delta^2\epsilon^2\leq k\log(ek/s)/n\). On every fixed infinite standard measurable space, the full nuisance-aware rate is matched because the minimax supremum may choose an \(n\)-dependent finitely supported \(P_X\) inside the unchanged space. Separately, on \([0,1]\) with \(P_X=\operatorname{Leb}\) itself fixed, a fine-partition sign mixture proves the same full matched rate. A singleton covariate space rules out a nuisance-product floor uniform over all fixed spaces, leaving only the sharp cardinality-dependent nuisance modulus for fixed finite spaces with at least two points open. Kramer--Kennedy--Opper is credited only for the sampling-lower mechanism; no nuisance-converse transfer is claimed. Conditional propensity zeros remain allowed in the universal class.
gap: Indirect provider excess is identified and has a fixed-provider efficient influence function. Kramer, Kennedy, and Opper's Theorem 1 supplies a sparse mean-potential-outcome upper bound, Theorem 2 its sampling lower bound, Theorem 3 a supplied-nuisance lower bound, and Theorem 4 a generic pseudo-outcome upper theorem, while their Section 7 leaves indirect excess for future work. No inspected result joins these pieces into a matched all-sample frontier for a random-denominator own-case-mix target under marginal provider balance, supplied simplex and marginal-outcome pilots, and conditional propensity zeros.
fill: The project supplies a feasible clipped empirical-ratio estimator, proves its sharp support-sensitive risk, and matches its sampling and nuisance components by lower bounds on the same supplied-pilot class. A fully specified \(k=72\), \(s=9\) law certifies that this class includes cases excluded by the weak-positivity setup of Kramer, Kennedy, and Opper's Theorem 4.
